title: Broad MGDA cross-seed logit ensemble feasibility
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: A frozen equal-logit ensemble of the three independently initialized half-dose MGDA residuals will cancel seed-specific policy drift while retaining learned opponent responses, producing a positive 16k-to-65k broad-holdout slope and outperforming the paired mean constituent at 65k without breaching Standard10 preservation.
material_change: At 16,384, 32,768, and 65,536 hands, load the three hash-verified half-dose residual checkpoints and form a frozen inference ensemble by averaging their logits and values. On wholly new common decks, evaluate the ensemble and all three constituents against the same three mixed-contract holdouts and both seats; share each Standard10 control rollout across candidates. Audit a fresh balanced source panel. No parameter update, Slumbot query, or new training hand is allowed.
baseline: The half-dose individual-seed curve preserved Standard10 but failed reproducibility: 16k-to-65k slopes +57.11, -18.34, -12.59 and matched full32k differences +7.05, -52.53, +1.76. The failure is seed/domain instability rather than trainer integrity.
notes: Admission requires all integrity checks; ensemble source agreement >=95% overall and >=90% in every partition at every dose; positive 16k-to-65k ensemble slope; nonnegative final pooled delta, at least two of three final holdouts and both seats; and positive paired final ensemble-minus-mean-constituent delta. This is feasibility only; a passing result requires independent-cohort replication before scale.

The all-slot max-delta gate reported exactly 64 because float32 averaging of three full logits perturbed the shared -1e9 illegal-action sentinel. Legal actions were still masked and the frozen game outcomes remain valid, but the wrapper fails the registered all-slot telemetry contract and must be repaired before reuse.

result.summary: Evaluated a frozen three-seed logit ensemble and all three constituents at 16k, 32k, and 65k on new common decks: 19,968 actual frozen games, 12,288 fresh source-panel queries, and zero training hands. The ensemble curve was -9.01, +3.95, and -18.20 bb/100; 16k-to-65k slope -9.19. At 65k only 1/3 holdouts and 1/2 seats were nonnegative, and paired gain versus the mean constituent was -12.49 bb/100. Source greedy agreement remained 99.37%, 98.73%, and 97.41%. All 254 tests passed.
result.conclusion: Cross-seed output averaging did not stabilize the broad-MGDA route: it worsened from 16k to 65k, underperformed the mean constituent, and failed pooled, holdout, and seat gates on untouched common decks. A separate telemetry flaw also shifted only masked illegal logits by 64 through float32 sentinel averaging. The performance evidence closes this ensemble route regardless of that diagnostic issue.
result.next_step: Repair and regression-test base-exact ensemble arithmetic without rerunning this closed performance route. Then move to a different learned-weight training mechanism rather than further composing the same unstable MGDA seeds.
